documents: Jiménez-Bonilla, Díaz-Azpiroz & Rodríguez Rodríguez (2023), Tectonics may affect closed watersheds used to monitor climate change and human activity effects, Terra Nova 35:58-65 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: tectonics acting at this same time scale has been overlooked when analysing endorheic systems, although it could eventually be a relevant controlling factor.

steps.action: The authors propose that playa lakes in closed watersheds, used as climate and human-impact indicators, may also respond to active tectonics.
steps.quote: but they could be also sensitive to active tectonics

steps.action: The authors pose the aim of evaluating how recent tectonics affected closed watersheds in the frontal fold-and-thrust belt of the western Betics, focusing on the El Gosque playa lake.
steps.quote: The main goal of this study is to evaluate the potential effect of recent tectonics on the evolution of some closed watersheds

steps.action: The authors adopt the χ-index expectation from Willett et al. (2014): basins with high χ are captured by neighbouring basins with lower χ.
steps.quote: Basins with larger χ values (victim) tend to be captured by basins with lower χ (aggressor)

steps.action: From the Andalusian DTM, revised in the field, the authors map the drainage network, stream profiles, the current flooded surface (43.3 hm2) and watershed (1198.7 hm2), and detect two knickpoints on the Albina stream.
steps.quote: Two knickpoints were detected along the Albina stream profile (K1 and K2; Figure 2b).

steps.action: The authors compare the current W/AFS ratio of 27.7 with the typical regional range for similar playa lakes taken from earlier studies.
steps.quote: clearly above the typical range (2.5–15) in similar playa

steps.action: From relief maps and topographic profiles, the authors reconstruct a paleo-shoreline at 425-430 m and a past flooded surface of 135.2 hm2.
steps.quote: Both relief maps and topographic profiles suggest that the EGP-L had a much bigger flooded surface (135.2 hm2) in the past

steps.action: The authors check the reconstructed paleo-shoreline against an independent trace: black soils found in soil profile surveys between the paleo and current shorelines.
steps.quote: The presence of black soils in the area between the paleo and current shorelines also points to this interpretation.

steps.action: The authors compute χ values for the drainage network: about 25 m for the Albina stream and 12 m for the La Fuente stream.
steps.quote: [...] a high disequilibrium between the Albina stream, which shows values of 25 m

steps.action: The authors compare the 13 m χ difference with the instability value of Willett et al. and infer an unstable divide, with La Fuente tending to capture the El Gosque watershed.
steps.quote: A difference of 13 m indicates that the water divide is extremely unstable

steps.action: The authors collect structural field data (fault planes, slickenlines, S-C structures) at both knickpoints and find that the knickpoints coincide with dextral strike-slip faults of the ABSZ.
steps.quote: Both knickpoints along the Albina stream spatially coincide with these dextral strike-slip faults.

steps.action: From the fault kinematics, the authors infer dominant dextral strike-slip to the west and a transtensive releasing bend with normal faults at the NE end.
steps.quote: The presence of normal faults to the NE end of the area is probably related to a transtensive releasing bend along the ABSZ

steps.action: Citing the absence of evidence for intense groundwater extraction or significant climate change over the last 2000 years, the authors exclude human and climatic causes of the lake shrinkage.
steps.quote: Therefore, the drastic water budget reduction for the EGP-L stems from another cause.

steps.action: The authors interpret the high Albina χ, knickpoint K1 and the stream elbow as a recent capture, and draw a paleo-drainage watershed of 3328 hm2 using K1 as the altitude reference.
steps.quote: Using K1 as the altitude reference, a tentative paleo-drainage watershed of the EGP-L is drawn

steps.action: The authors compare the paleo W/AFS ratio (24.6) with the current one (27.7) and conclude that the shrinkage came from a loss of watershed area, not a change in the input/output balance.
steps.quote: This suggests that the input/output ratio of the basin did not varied significantly during the AFS reduction

steps.action: Using cited archaeological evidence of Roman settlements and lake sediments, the authors attribute knickpoint K2 to a second capture and date the reshaping of the El Gosque watershed to post-Roman times.
steps.quote: would have occurred in post-Roman times (younger than 1600 years BP).

steps.action: The authors keep the attribution of the successive captures, and of the watersheds' elongation and evolution, to active fault segments of the ABSZ.
steps.quote: The NE–SW elongation of these drainage watersheds and their evolution are probably controlled by active segments of the ABSZ.

steps.action: From the χ contrasts, the authors project future captures of the endorheic areas by La Fuente and the Mediterranean rivers, and tentatively attribute the basins' preservation to transpressive uplift.
steps.quote: The preservation of these basins is tentatively assigned to recent tectonic activity.

steps.action: The authors conclude that local uplift may favour stream capture that reduces closed-watershed inputs, and that tectonics must be considered when closed basins are used to monitor climate and human impacts.
steps.quote: This work reveals that tectonics should be also considered when assessing the role of human activity and/or climate change

tree.answer: Shrinkage of the El Gosque playa-lake flooded surface and watershed, linked to stream capture
No; the past lake extent is inferred from topography and soils, and the captures from knickpoints and χ
Evaluate the effect of recent tectonics on the evolution of closed watersheds
Human groundwater extraction, climate change, and tectonically favoured stream capture
Only weakly: a near-constant W/AFS ratio is taken to favour area loss over a water-balance change
Conditions found: past captures known only from traces
Partly: one independent trace (black soils) and cited archaeology; no sensitivity tests
Tectonically favoured capture kept as the hedged best explanation
Two anonymous referees are acknowledged; no review file was supplied

end.claim: Local tectonic uplift along active ABSZ fault segments probably favoured stream captures that reduced the El Gosque watershed area and its water inputs, shrinking the playa lake to about a third of its past flooded area; tectonics should therefore be considered when closed basins are used to monitor climate and human impacts.

decisive_move.sentence: Reconstructing the paleo-drainage watershed from knickpoint K1, and comparing its W/AFS ratio with the present one, is what links the lake shrinkage to watershed loss by stream capture.

gates.evidence: Structural data were collected at faults spatially associated with the knickpoints, an acquisition directed by the tectonic hypothesis (p. 60), but the geomorphic mapping was not hypothesis-directed. The W/AFS comparison (p. 63) could in principle have failed. The rivals were excluded only by citing an absence of evidence (pp. 62-63). Nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Roman settlement survey (Recio-Ruiz & Ruíz-Somovilla 1990), used to date the separate lake and the capture

novelty_claims.quote: together with structural and other geomorphic analyses such as the χ index, never before has it been made to detect active structures
none of them have analysed the possible evolution of the watersheds due to active tectonics until the present study.
The endorheic area we chose to apply this new approach

limits: The paleo-shoreline, the black soils and the captures are not dated; timing rests on cited archaeology, so the post-Roman age is inferred. The χ calculation parameters (A0, m/n) and their sensitivity are not reported, and no robustness tests are shown. The human and climate rivals are excluded only by citing an absence of evidence over the last 2000 years, without new data. The tectonic link rests on spatial coincidence of knickpoints with faults; no fault ages or slip rates are given, so causation is inferred. Human infrastructure is acknowledged as an influence but not quantified. Sub-claims at other statuses: fault kinematics and the transtensive releasing bend (best_explanation); future captures by La Fuente and the Mediterranean rivers, and preservation of the basins by uplift, are qualitative projections described as tentative (none). No review file was supplied, so the effect of the two referees acknowledged on p. 64 cannot be coded (inference: the manuscript was revised, received 2021 and revised 2022).

disagreements.target: Literature attributing short-term hydrological change in closed basins to human activities, and longer-term change to climate
disagreements.support: The authors argue that capture favoured by tectonics can reduce playa-lake flooded area where neither human extraction nor climate change is evidenced.
disagreements.quote: hydrological modifications in the short term (hundreds of years) have been traditionally attributed to human activities

disagreements.target: Environmental studies of southern Spanish playa lakes (Höbig et al. 2016; Rodríguez-Rodríguez et al. 2010-2021 and others)
disagreements.support: The authors show a case where watershed evolution driven by tectonics, not considered in those studies, controls the water budget.
disagreements.quote: none of them have analysed the possible evolution of the watersheds due to active tectonics until the present study.

disagreements.target: Elez et al. (2016, 2018) regional post-Messinian uplift as the control on divide instability
disagreements.support: The coincidence of knickpoints with active ABSZ fault segments is offered as evidence that small local structures also matter.
disagreements.quote: smaller sized active structures within the western Betics FTB play a crucial role on the Atlantic-Mediterranean divide instability

alternatives_considered.chosen: Reduction in water input from loss of watershed area by stream capture
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Intense human groundwater extraction for agriculture; significant climate change over the last 2000 years
alternatives_considered.reason: No evidence in the area for either (cited Höbig et al. 2016; Martín-Puertas et al. 2010)
